machine: Windows 10, Intel64 Family 6 Model 183 Stepping 1, GenuineIntel
backend: MJX on JAX CPU (jaxlib has no CUDA wheel for native Windows)
protocol: WalkerRagdoll model, frame_skip=5, dt/action=0.010s, ctrl U(-0.5,0.5), 4.0s steady-state per size, nconmax=512 njmax=4096

cpu_reference.note: parallel path is 32 worker processes; ~130us of serial parent-side pickle work per env per vector step is the ceiling

verdict.question: Does MJX beat envs/parallel_vector_env.py (MuJoCo-C worker processes) for WalkerRagdoll-v0?
verdict.answer: NO on this hardware, at every batch size measured, on CPU and on GPU.
why: MJX is dense: walker_ragdoll.xml has 138 geom pairs and all 138 are collision-tested and solved every mj_step, while MuJoCo-C measured ncon=3 in the same fallen state. The solver works on ~46x more constraint rows than the sparse path needs.

The committed model is RK4, which costs 4 force evaluations per mj_step: measured at nworld=512 on the RTX 4070 Laptop, RK4+postconstraint gives 935 env-steps/s and Euler gives 3,828, so RK4 alone is a ~4x tax. Switching integrator changes the dynamics, so it is not a free tuning knob.
mjx.rne_postconstraint, needed for cfrc_ext/impact_cost, costs ~24% at nworld=512 (935 -> 1,231 env-steps/s without it). mjx.step does not compute cfrc_ext, exactly like mj_step.

MJX-CPU throughput is flat-to-worse with batch size (31.6 env-steps/s at nworld=32, 22.9 at 128): a vmap'd XLA graph on one CPU device does not gain from more worlds, it just divides the same throughput.
MJX-GPU saturates near 1,275 env-steps/s from nworld=512 onward; even the relaxed-Euler best case at nworld=1024 reaches only 4,338, still 1.5x below the committed CPU path.
verdict.gpu_status: Measured for real: WSL2 Ubuntu-24.04 with jax-cuda12-plugin on the RTX 4070 Laptop (8 GB, XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.6). Native Windows jaxlib is CPU-only.

conclusion: MJX-CPU is ~200x slower than the committed process-parallel path; do not adopt.
